The airfoil configurations were modeled with 20-node isoparametric 3D finite elements, with 46 elements and 405 nodes for the leading-edge film-cooled airfoil and 39 elements and 349 nodes for the all-impingement cooled airfoil.

The assumed flight mission consisted of a 5-second transient from idle to maximum takeoff, 5-minute hold at max takeoff, 30-minute hold at max climb, 90-minute hold at cruise, and 5-second transient back to idle.
At maximum takeoff, the gas inlet total pressure was 2858 kPa and the coolant-to-gas flow ratio was 0.116 to 0.118.
The maximum metal temperature reached during the mission was about 1050°C, occurring at maximum takeoff.

The critical location for maximum creep strain was at the inside wall of the leading edge region at 33% span height for the all-impingement cooled cases, and adjacent to the film cooling hole rim for the film-cooled cases.
Compared to the all-impingement cooled configuration, leading-edge film cooling increased the creep strain range by 100% and the total strain range by 230% for the mission cycle.
Angling the film cooling holes 30 degrees radially resulted in 20% lower creep life penalty compared to holes normal to the surface.
Fatigue life predictions indicated the fatigue lives would be at least an order of magnitude greater than the predicted creep lives for the film-cooled cases.
The one-dimensional beam-type analyses predicted somewhat higher initial creep strains but exaggerated the amount of stress relaxation compared to the 3D finite element results.
